missionPremise: OPS-21's publish gate currently grades 17 of the 65 closed parcel-record rails (SLATE_1+1B+1C+1D+LANDUSE_OWNER_GATE_GAP). Canon requires 'unaccounted' to be fatal at publish; for 48 of 65 rails that requirement is unenforced in code. D5's ruling: widen DEFAULT_SCHED_RAIL_KEYS in publish-gate-sched.mjs to derive from the closed rail set (rail-keys.js, PARCEL_RECORD_RAIL_KEYS, 65) rather than the hand-built five-slate union, on the stated premise that grading is not serving and this is customer-invisible.
premiseCorrection:
The dispatch's STANDING FACTS claim ('widening the gate produces refuse verdicts ... and changes nothing a customer sees') is TRUE for parcelRecordAllowlist.ts (legacy-design-tools), the LDT serve-side allowlist, and FALSE for this repo's own pre-bake publish gate, which the dispatch did not name. Verified at source, not assumed:

1. src/lib/publish-readiness-gate.mjs:319 and :359 (pre-fix) both defaulted `requiredRails` to the SAME imported `DEFAULT_SCHED_RAIL_KEYS` symbol from publish-gate-sched.mjs.
2. src/jobs/bastrop-publish.mjs:407-410 calls `requirePreBakeReadiness({ factory, neondb, mcp }, flags.county)` with NO third argument -- the default is load-bearing in production. The module's own doc line 75 says this runs 'Executes: runBastropPublish, after resolveTargetStores and before the first bake, both targets' and line 76 'Triggers: every publish, any target, any county.'
3. evaluatePreBakeReadiness (publish-readiness-gate.mjs:319-347, pre-fix numbering) throws RAIL_UNACCOUNTED for any required rail with no parcel_gate_verdict row, and RAIL_REFUSED for any required rail whose verdict is 'refuse' -- this is a hard fail-CLOSED throw, unlike parcelRecordAllowlist.ts's fail-soft 'refused'-state serve fallback.
4. Live read-only query against parcel_gate_verdict (FACTORY_DATABASE_URL_RO, 2026-09-10): of the 48 rails NOT in the pre-D5 17-rail DEFAULT_SCHED_RAIL_KEYS, 46 carry ZERO verdict rows across all six counties, and 'schoolDistrict' (one of the two that already has rows) carries 6 rows: 3 'pass' / 3 'refuse'. Total table state: 110 rows, 19 distinct rail_key values (the 17 pre-D5 defaults plus 'agValuation' [2 rows, both pass] and 'schoolDistrict' [6 rows, 3 refuse] from prior manual/out-of-band runs), all six counties present (48021, 48055, 48209, 48309, 48453, 48491).

Conclusion: a literal widen-only implementation (repoint DEFAULT_SCHED_RAIL_KEYS to the 65-rail derived set with no other change) would, the moment it deploys, make bastrop-publish.mjs's pre-bake gate immediately refuse EVERY publish for EVERY county -- 46 rails RAIL_UNACCOUNTED plus schoolDistrict RAIL_REFUSED in 3 of 6 counties, all pre-existing in the table today, none requiring a scheduler run to trigger. This is a production regression to the Factory's own bake pipeline, not a customer-facing regression, and it is NOT something this lane could then fix, since 'fixing any rail that now refuses' is explicitly out of scope for D5.
schoolDistrictReconciliation: Checked precisely per operator request, cross-repo (read-only, AGENT_CONTRACT section on cross-repo reads): legacy-design-tools origin/main, artifacts/api-server/src/lib/parcelRecordAllowlist.ts. schoolDistrict IS in PARCEL_RECORD_SLATE for all six counties (module doc, 'schoolDistrict, ALL SIX counties including Caldwell (F-01, serve/prod cutover, 2026-09-04)'). resolveAllowlistState (parcelRecordAllowlist.ts:351-359): a slated pair with a non-pass verdict returns 'refused', and 'refused' behaves identically to 'legacy' at the serve layer (old path, nothing from parcel_record) -- confirmed at parcelRecordAllowlist.ts:356-359. So schoolDistrict's 3 live refuse verdicts are SAFE and BY DESIGN on the LDT/customer-serving side (matches the dispatch's claim exactly) -- the two claims that looked contradictory are about two different gates reading the same table with opposite failure semantics: LDT fails soft (serve legacy), hauska-factory's own publish-readiness-gate fails hard (throws, refuses the bake). Only the second is a real hazard, and only for this repo's own pipeline, never for what a customer sees.
decision:
Implement the mission literally for the scheduler (DEFAULT_SCHED_RAIL_KEYS derived from PARCEL_RECORD_RAIL_KEYS, length 65, exported from publish-gate-sched.mjs -- satisfies the completion predicate's first clause exactly) AND decouple the pre-bake publish gate's required-rail default from that widened constant, per explicit operator/user ruling on this exact question (AskUserQuestion, 2026-09-10, 'Option A -- decouple', with three refinements, all applied):

1. New export PUBLISH_FLOOR_RAIL_KEYS in publish-readiness-gate.mjs, documented as a POLICY FLOOR (a deliberate, code-owned subset, the same kind of artifact as PARCEL_RECORD_SLATE) rather than a frozen snapshot of the old DEFAULT_SCHED_RAIL_KEYS -- seeded at exactly the five pre-D5 slates (17 rails), all independently verified clean (0 refuse, 0 unaccounted, all six counties) as of 2026-09-10.
2. Load-time assertion that every PUBLISH_FLOOR_RAIL_KEYS entry is a member of PARCEL_RECORD_RAIL_KEYS (rail-keys.js) -- a typo'd floor rail fails at import, not by silently gating on a phantom key.
3. Header comment states explicitly this floor is expected to GROW, names the expansion path (a later OPS-21 lane adds a rail here once its writer is verified clean across all six counties -- a ruling, not silent inheritance from DEFAULT_SCHED_RAIL_KEYS widening again), and is not a permanent carve-out.
4. evaluatePreBakeReadiness and requirePreBakeReadiness (publish-readiness-gate.mjs) now default `requiredRails` to PUBLISH_FLOOR_RAIL_KEYS, not DEFAULT_SCHED_RAIL_KEYS. bastrop-publish.mjs is UNCHANGED (still calls with no override) and therefore genuinely unaffected -- it now resolves to the floor, which is byte-identical in membership to what it resolved to before this lane touched anything.

The five slate constants (SLATE_1_RAIL_KEYS etc.) are retained unchanged; their union is retained under a new name (SLATE_1_THROUGH_LANDUSE_OWNER_UNION) since 'DEFAULT_SCHED_RAIL_KEYS' no longer means that union.
